title: liver
notes: NL: a completely different transcription is given in the response to question 471: [g′r′iːʃḳ′iːn′iː], 'gríscíní' perhaps, though Wagner has a question mark next to it. Ó Dónaill gives this as meaning slices of meat. The transcription on the map, along with those for points 53-59, was difficult to translate into orthography. Art Hughes has this one as ‘aobhachaí’, but that doesn’t match this point’s pronunciation of <aobh>, see map 177a. Of course, incomplete sound changes can result in such disrepancies, but I do wonder if this has a different form etymologically, particularly given how old a pronunciation of <ao> as a diphthong would be (I will note that Wagner doesn’t really segment syllables which can make some of these transcriptions ambiguous RE diphthongs). Dinneen has ‘aedhanna’ for the plural of ‘ae’. I have gone with something in that vein, despite it breaking some modern spelling conventions. I am open to suggestions.

Writing <ae> for the initial [əj] fits with other areas, but it then becomes difficult to write something conventional. See also note on point 33.
